correctness.rationale: For normalized Bergman monomials e_k=z^k/s_k, s_k²=Γ(α+2)Γ(k+1)/Γ(k+α+2), the adjoint gives T e_{nk}=β_k e_{mk}, β_k=s_{mk}s_{nk}/s_k², all other basis vectors to zero. For distinct divisible m,n≥2, t=max/min≥2, every positive multiple of the smaller degree belongs to a unique ray indexed by h with t∤h. If n=mt, the arrows run toward smaller indices (weighted backward shift); if m=nt, they run outward (weighted forward shift). Γ-ratio asymptotics imply β_k/c=1+O(1/k), c=(mn)^(-(α+1)/2), and |log(β_{ht^j}/c)|≤B/(ht^j). Sum over all j≤J is ≤Bt/(h(t-1)), uniformly in ray and J. This yields bounded invertible global diagonal conjugacy to countably many cS* or cS summands, alongside a scalar 1 and infinite zero block. Classical shift point/residual/continuous spectral facts, amplified by infinite multiplicity, give the precise disk, the Fredholm-essential disk and the orientation-dependent interior type. At the unit-circle boundary shifted shifts are injective and dense-range but not surjective. The essential norm is NOT deduced from similarity: replacing disjoint arrow weights β_k by c is compact (β_k→c), with a rank-one constant adjustment, and infinitely many orthogonal arrows give essential norm c. α>-1, m≠n, c<1 are used; nothing is claimed for unrelated degrees.
